confirmedIssues: PKCE verifier truncates 28 random 32-bit words to 56 hex digits, retaining at most 224 random bits rather than the recommended 256; both original JavaScript blocks reproduced this. S256 hashing itself passes the RFC test vector.

Original jwt.decode calls accept missing exp/iat/sub and missing or wrong nonce; azp and untrusted additional audiences also need application/profile checks. Missing sub raises KeyError in the later print, not a validation success.
Authentication table overgeneralizes ID tokens; authorization code is wrongly restricted to confidential clients; client credentials does not always make the client the resource owner.
ROPC recommendation must reflect RFC 9700 MUST NOT; implicit access-token response guidance must retain its conditions and normative strength.
JWT three-part structure applies to JWS Compact, not all JWTs; signing is not encryption or generic public-key decryption. Signature inputs need explicit bytes and algorithm semantics.
ID-token decoding is not authentication; claim presence, issuer-scoped subject identity, transaction nonce, trusted key acquisition and callback bindings need explanation.
Expiry alone is not validity; iat plus lifetime is equivalent only with the stated exp construction; refresh issuance and revocation behavior depend on the design.
